claims.statement: MDR requires manufacturers to operate a planned, documented and continuous PMS system integrated with the quality system.
Class IIa/IIb PSURs must summarize PMS analysis, benefit-risk conclusions, preventive and corrective actions and device sales or usage denominators.
Current MDCG guidance explicitly links complaints and service information with exposure, trend thresholds, risk management and CAPA, supporting the proposed lineage job.
MDCG PSUR guidance standardizes report content and cadence, making parts of the artifact reproducible rather than proprietary.
PRRC duties require formal qualifications and reside with qualified persons available to the manufacturer, so vendor software cannot own regulatory compliance authority.
MDR serious-incident reporting deadlines include two, ten and fifteen days depending on urgency and severity.
Four EUDAMED modules became mandatory on 28 May 2026, while PMS and vigilance remained under development, leaving workflow space without creating a private platform gate.
Complaint data can include special-category health data and requires a lawful basis, minimization, security and defined controller-processor responsibilities.
MasterControl and Greenlight Guru already sell integrated post-market workflows spanning complaints, risk, CAPA and reporting.
The 38,000-plus European medtech-company count and roughly 90% SME share is a broad sector denominator, not evidence for the reachable Class IIa/IIb target segment.
The only plausible distinct control point is validated lineage across complaint, denominator, trend, risk/CAPA and PSUR approval; generic intake or drafting is readily bundled or reproduced.
Paid willingness to adopt a separate lineage layer, representative evidence gaps and measured review-time or audit-quality improvement are unknown.
Customer-specific validation cost, consultant channel commitment, CAC, sales cycle, churn and support burden are unknown.

contrary_evidence: Qualified PRRC and manufacturer personnel hold the necessary authority.
MasterControl and Greenlight Guru already bundle much of the proposed workflow.
MDCG guidance standardizes the required artifact and reduces scarcity.
EUDAMED's evolving modules may absorb parts of the workflow.
GDPR and validation duties restrict reuse of sensitive complaint data and increase service burden.
